changes: Added eight authored battle opening camera paths with a smooth handoff into combat, protected input/timers, reduced-motion options and safe camera fallbacks.

Rebuilt battle scenery around the approved backgrounds with separate ground, banks and distant depth surfaces, matching solid rocks and rooted edge trees. Camera moves reveal depth while the cast stays grounded.

Added restrained water and waterfall motion, wind-blown foliage and fine grass. Removed oversized mismatched scenery, bright ground blobs and distracting foreground clutter while preserving all twenty day/night stage pairs.
Introduced twelve distinct rock forms, connected tree growth and a shared light-responsive water treatment across the overworld and local scenes.
Brought the battle, day/night and scene testers into a password-gated developer console hidden in the changelog. Its toolbar stays at the top and adapts to portrait and landscape phones.
Improved phone layouts, safe areas, scrolling and orientation changes across menus, tester controls, dialogue and combat.
Allowed the party to pass NPCs and individual overworld trees while preserving building, water, local-tree and continent boundary collision.
Kept scenery opaque and added an animated player silhouette when the controlled character is behind buildings or trees.
Removed the loading screen outer frame and the custom F fullscreen shortcut. F11 remains available through the browser.
Removed dialogue-advance click sounds, unified E interaction prompts and gave world narration a centered, frameless presentation.
Added matching quest icons above relevant NPCs and on the minimap, with acceptance/completion updates independent of compass tracking.
Reduced repeated scene preparation by reusing vegetation, route and boundary data, stable light slots and compiled material families.
Preserved the approach side when entering or leaving POIs through named entrances; corrected arrival and return points across all fifteen destinations.
Unified standard enemy defeat dissolves and sprite-colored particles. Defeated enemies immediately stop acting and cannot be targeted; rewards remain once-only.
Integrated ten approved ability-type icons and eighteen buff, debuff and status icons, with turn badges, descriptions and an accessible in-game legend.
Enemy weaknesses now begin hidden and are learned only through successful matching hits. Discoveries are tracked separately for each enemy and type during the current battle.

First discoveries trigger a brief confirmation and the attacking character’s own queued voice reaction. Matching discovered weaknesses show WEAK during ability targeting without leaking unknown affinities.
Polished damage and healing numbers with clear outlines, distinct healing treatment, controlled impact motion and camera-following actor anchors. Rapid hits receive separated positions.
Aligned combat with the approved HUD: compact turn portraits above, commands and Skills in the upper right, smaller tightly spaced party cards below, and contextual help clear of the timing meter.
Formal story objectives and optional quests now grant EXP plus curated randomized loot alongside guaranteed rewards. Saved completion receipts prevent duplicate grants.
Added seven consumable magical combat gems: Fire, Ice, Water, Lightning, Wind, Earth and Poison. Rewards display EXP, items and quantities clearly.

releaseNotes.title: A clearer world, richer maps and distinct battles
items: Rebuilt the traversal landscape with subtle rolling ground, valleys and mountain ranges. POI foundations, roads, coastlines and the 3D atlas now share the terrain.
Made overworld bridges cross real water with submerged riverbeds, dry approaches and walkable decks.
Replanned all fifteen POIs with larger connected streets, service courts and clearer boundaries. Moved wilderness destinations away from town miniatures and improved building orientation.
Matched invisible boundaries to the expanded pathways. Denser, irregular forests, mixed tree ages and mountain edges blend the impassable areas into the environment.
Made POI departures, overworld destination entry and building doors deliberate E interactions, with contextual prompts and scene fades instead of automatic transfers.
Grounded buildings, pedestals and crystals across their whole footprint, corrected buried structures and reduced flickering landmark surfaces.
Made visible residents available for conversation even outside their current story action, without advancing quests or granting rewards through idle dialogue.
Smoothed overworld party movement and kept the camera centered on the traveling party. Preserved collision-aware companions and scene-return positions.
Reskinned the world map and shared menus with native PixelLab navy-and-gold artwork, illustrated headers, ornamental frames, buttons and backgrounds.
Refined the settlement picker and navigation shortcuts. Town silhouettes remain visible before discovery while local interiors, services and unexplored details stay hidden until learned.
Rebuilt the north-up minimap with a matching gold compass, consistent live icons, a complete icon legend, zoom and a time-and-weather strip. Minimap clicks open the local map; M opens the world map.
Made quest guidance depend on explicitly tracking a quest. Limited recorded voice requests to combat moves and prevented text or artwork selection during play.
Added twenty regional PixelLab battle environments, including ten distinct grasslands, each with matching day and night art: forty native 688 by 384 backgrounds.
Moved random encounters into separate staged scenes with a flat combat floor, aligned actor feet and contact shadows. Battle return restores the exploration scene and party position.
Authored continuous predawn, dawn, morning, noon, afternoon, golden-hour, dusk and moonlight palettes for POIs and the overworld, with readable night paths, party silhouettes and nearby landmarks.
Added depth-aware atmosphere, foliage light and sun rays filtered by actual cloud cover and scene shadows. Softened cloud shadows and stabilized shadow projections during movement.
Fixed repeated cloud and sunlight shader decoration that caused growing shader counts and stutter. Reused shadow allocations and verified stable shader counts during sustained play.
Removed gameplay lens blur and prevented aggressive render-resolution reductions. Retained live lighting, rays, weather, shadows, battle controls and responsive phone layouts.

releaseNotes.title: Purposeful paths and a grounded party
items: Replanned all fifteen POIs around connected main paths, service approaches, story courts and clear road-aligned exits. Natural stone, shrubs and trees define the playable routes.

Kept the approved atlas placement and story targets while removing empty outer road tails and random outskirts housing. Cleared obstructing route trees and painted the existing terrain across detail levels.
Preserved exact approach chains in navigation so distant exits and story interactions remain connected. Legacy arrivals settle safely inside the new routes.

Required movement into a doorway for automatic entry; street routes to other destinations no longer enter buildings accidentally. Actors can move out of a pre-existing crowd overlap while still respecting personal space.
Made companions keep pace with Shift sprinting while following their own collision-safe trail and running animation.
Interpolated wind and weather motion at presentation time and refreshed directional shadows for moving foliage and actors on every presented frame.
Strengthened ground-conforming underfoot shadows on streets, bridges, stairs and indoor floors.
Preserved ambient wildlife habitats outside the public paths and kept new boundary props clear of their roaming routes.

releaseNotes.title: Smoother motion, water and light
items: Synchronized camera and character interpolation across display refresh rates to remove landscape judder while running.
Bounded simulation catch-up after long stalls, reused exact terrain queries within each step, and removed a duplicate flat foot-shadow layer.
Replaced layered river geometry rewrites with one cached row update and completed the downstream refill through the end of the channel.
Prevented water surfaces and mist reflecting back into neighboring water targets; restored transforms after every reflection pass.
Updated moving directional shadows every presented frame and retained the matching projection when reusing a stationary shadow map.

Anchored atmospheric scattering to fixed distance intervals with softened shadow sampling. Added denser world-space dust that responds to canopy and cloud shadows, with stable seeds across cell boundaries.

releaseNotes.title: Steadier surfaces in motion
items: Stopped terrain, trees, ground foliage and their shadows repeatedly changing detail when movement hovered around a distance threshold. Wider entry/exit bands preserve adaptive rendering without rapid visual switches.
Replaced discontinuous atmospheric ray-sampling noise with continuous world-space variation, reducing movement-triggered brightness flashes without increasing scattering steps.

releaseNotes.title: A world shaped by its atlas
items: Rebuilt atlas relief, coastal shelves and northern mountains with naturally blended climate transitions. Restored the green region’s Valenne and Brook rivers; replaced the desert cuts with winding tributaries, an oasis and one connected coastal outlet.
Moved the southern volcanic island farther offshore and south; its coastal harbor keeps its position on the moved island.
Replaced sparse map canopies and patterned ocean water with fuller native forests, depth-based coastal color and a whole-world view.
Rebuilt Fern woodland houses as covered timber pavilions, strengthened Highmere civic silhouettes, and dressed the relief and shelter courts.
Replaced the outdoor meadow in the Fern remnant with a textured stone vault and ancient spindle mechanism. Removed inherited houses from wilderness patrols, ruins and Elder Light clearings.
Added monument pedestals, weathered ruin arches, natural outcrops and roadside flower drifts while reserving road shoulders and story interaction space.
Integrated a new 512-pixel PixelLab cliff texture and matching normal map, with triplanar cliff mapping to avoid stretched rock stripes.
Joined overworld crossings with continuous banks and physical bridge approaches. Verified all 15 destinations against atlas positions and usable trail thresholds.

Gave each POI a natural JRPG perimeter with clear openings, glowing floor arrows at actual doors and trail mouths, and walking or E transitions. Overworld entry spots sit beside the road instead of on shrines.
Fixed Fern’s riverbank exit and E targeting at doors beside villagers. Added snow on foliage, alternating snow tracks and pooled contact shadows directly beneath visible characters and creatures.
Integrated a new 512-pixel PixelLab river current texture and subtle normal map. Water junctions share one triangulated surface; continuous shaped banks replace square traced channels.

releaseNotes.title: A steadier journey and a more distinct world
items: Fixed simulation timing so movement, combat and the day cycle keep their pace when presentation frame rates change. Fixed scene and water-shader cleanup found during long travel/combat sessions, and reduced redundant terrain and transform work on slower devices.
Added versioned journey records with stable quest identities, validation, recovery copies and portable file import/export for the three record slots.
Rebuilt campaign work actions with route recovery and visible helpers. The regional restoration visits all four repaired Elder Lights in saved order and can resume after loading.

Added encounter-specific rewards, speed-based turns, readable enemy intentions, weaknesses, stagger and consistent level growth. Protected the coached opening battle from premature defeats and repeated demonstration clicks.
Built distinct pitched woodland homes and pale-stone civic architecture from the current Drive concepts. Updated the atlas to 25 named places and modeled its three sourced coastal harbor landmarks.
Added seven approved-concept creature families, complete directional motion, larger native artwork for giant creatures, and physical species scales shared by exploration and combat.

Added detailed native stone and woodland materials with lighting normal maps, regional ElevenLabs ambience and creature foley. Local requests now include named gathering, delivery, repair and recording work.
Improved exploration camera framing, kept selected-enemy outlines thin at large creature sizes, and aligned attack effects with each target’s physical height.

releaseNotes.title: Faster starts, smaller memory and steadier play
items: Added a functional staged loader for reading the bundled file, decoding artwork and short sounds, compiling lighting, preparing weather, uploading textures and warming geometry before play.
Baked the actual overworld height field and tree positions. The 3D atlas keeps the same geography without retaining the continent’s close-up grass and canopy buffers.
Fixed departed scenes being retained by shader-material callbacks. Compiled programs now use a bounded cache; replaced party canvases and materials are released.
Shared immutable foliage buffers, reused native character planes, enlarged meadow batches and culled static branches with reflection and shadow coverage preserved.
Combined world-anchored rain and snow into one draw, prepared location weather samples behind loading screens and bounded overworld weather prefetch.
Added startup graphics calibration, constrained-device shadow/reflection cadence and appropriate render-target budgets. CPU pressure no longer needlessly blurs the scene.
Removed duplicate minimap rendering, cached unchanged party cards and radar content, accelerated fog-of-war records and removed redundant simulation catch-up work.
Prepared recorded voice URLs and decoded short effects before gameplay. All existing PixelLab art, detailed textures, abilities, lighting, saves and story content remain available.

releaseNotes.title: Elemental power, natural creatures and living light
items: Rebuilt the wolf and boar combat profiles with new PixelLab side-view art, breathing, lunging, recoil and recovery poses. All native frames retain consistent scale and transparent borders.
Added six high resolution PixelLab effect textures for fire slashes, impacts, arcane lightning, frost, healing and smoke, animated as depth-tested world geometry with real effect lights.
Added pooled soft contact shadows beneath visible party members, residents and creatures, alongside their dynamic directional shadows.
Integrated cloud- and shadow-aware volumetric scattering with world-anchored shafts, luminous dust, warm dawn and golden-hour light.
Batched hundreds of bridge support stones while retaining authored walking decks, collision and texture blends.
Reduced repeated particle-buffer uploads and temporary effect allocations; retained bounded pools and tiered terrain, foliage, shadow and rendering budgets.

releaseNotes.title: Warmer light, steadier frames, a journey in your hand
items: Rebalanced the continuous solar cycle with amber dawn and golden hour, clear midday, readable blue moonlight, glowing windows and warm light reaching nearby surfaces across the scene.
Added depth-aware lens focus that keeps the party and playable middle ground sharp, with a consistent blur radius across display densities.
Extended meadow coverage to 185 metres in locations and 230 metres on the overworld, with lower-detail distant foliage and conservative spatial visibility.
Coalesced window and orientation changes, removed resolution-dependent shadow-map thrashing and kept shadow, reflection and scene buffers within stable budgets.
Added CPU/GPU-aware detail tiers and render scaling with slow recovery, refresh-divisor pacing and fixed light slots to avoid compiling a new lighting variant during attacks.
Character textures now upload only the current native frame on an individual canvas, preserving the authored pixels, frame borders, facing and separate character sizes.
Enlarged foliage batches, cached bounded live road queries and tightened scene resource cleanup for repeated travel and extended play.

Rebuilt compact portrait and landscape layouts with journey shortcuts, expandable objectives, compact party cards, a touch joystick, sprint toggle and interaction button. Touch cancellation clears held movement.

Added larger separated touch targets for enemy selection and kept the full battle in frame in portrait mode. Strengthened pooled attack lights and highlight bloom so abilities illuminate the actual environment.

releaseNotes.title: Clearer routes, steady characters and flowing water
items: Removed the mismatched front-facing Soren idle poses while preserving the complete native coat animation.
Kept physical bridge decks visible through scene trimming and cutaways, and extended terrain beneath enlarged approaches.
Removed stray neighbouring road strips, continued roads past exit markers and rerouted the Network approach around its cliff.
Matched walking heights to the fine road surfaces and removed road-blocking rocks without a valid relocation.
Restricted the remnant rock overhang to its own location, reserved full road clearance and moved noticeboards to walkable shoulders with collision only while visible.
Slowed the sluice release and downstream recovery; water now clears the stone sill before the lower pools fill.
Removed the sweeping current ribbon and obsolete spray, with slower flowing surface and cascade textures.
Replaced overlapping old cloud planes with a bounded, rounded cloud volume linked to the moving sun, shadows and light shafts.
Cleaned up previous weather chunks during repeated setup and kept outdoor light, dust and cloud colours tied to the day/night cycle.

releaseNotes.title: A moving sky, a better-built world
items: The sun now crosses the sky from east to west. Fourteen smoothly blended colour keys tint direct light, sky, clouds, ambient fill, haze, shafts and dust: violet predawn, peach sunrise, blue midday, amber golden hour, rose dusk and cool moonlight.
Moving volumetric clouds share one world-space field with surface shadows, sunlight shafts and airborne dust. Clouds interrupt the light, while persistent rays stay anchored in the landscape.

Rebuilt settlement facades with recessed doors, fitted awnings, complete roof ends, framed windows, properly seated chimneys and clear entry steps. Removed overlapping inn additions and duplicate facade layers.
Forest homes now have closed curved roof ends and fitted porches. Relief pavilions have colliders around real posts, rear panels and furniture, allowing passage under the open canopy.
Rearranged shop and smithy shelving, weapon displays and service counters. Back doors remain clear, and the aid office now has its own desk, waiting area and storage.

Window light changes at dusk. Outdoor pollen, night fireflies, cool ambient fill and cloud-filtered sunbeams respond to the continuous clock and weather. Loading stills show the rebuilt in-game village and rooms.

releaseNotes.title: Living gardens, clearer light
items: Fixed trees failing to reveal the party: every foliage detail level now shares the same individual-tree cutaway mask, while real shadows and water reflections retain the complete tree.
Rebuilt the forest as branched 3D crowns of folded, transparent PixelLab leaf sprays. Oaks, birches, maples, willows, spruces and flowering trees vary in shape, height, colour and placement.
Added five flower forms, curved grass tufts, folded ferns and leafy shrubs, planted in stable roadside and garden clusters. Removed the black distant shrub geometry.

Integrated 17 native 512px PixelLab assets, including paving, mossy paving, slate, plaster and meadow textures with matching normal maps. Material scale makes individual stones and roof courses more readable.
Moved the sun to illuminate building fronts, balanced warm sunlight against cool fill, reduced pale haze and broad additive rays, and preserved fine detail through gentler focus and bloom.
Adjusted the exploration lens for a closer diorama view with a slight diagonal angle. Forest batching uses larger cells and shared detail levels; loading stills now show the current in-game artwork.

Optimized live water reflections with a cropped reflected view that draws only scenery sampled by visible water, preserving the full projective image and immediate updates. Inactive botanical detail levels are released during travel.

releaseNotes.title: A warmer welcome indoors
items: Rebuilt all seven active interiors with a closer, front-facing camera pitched down 25 degrees, including responsive tracking on narrow screens.

Added four native PixelLab interior assets: chestnut wall panels, detailed hearth stone, a woven rug and framed riverland artwork. Stocked shelves, table settings, chairs, banners and plants bring the rooms to life.
Added an open, animated fireplace and warm pooled lighting that affects characters and furnishings. Counter heights keep hosts readable, with clear routes to services, exits and inn save seals.
Fixed the missing objective for A choice of restraint. Tavin now has a visible encounter seal and affected villagers at the gathering ground; the marker clears after victory.
Replaced the old loading still with four fresh 1080p captures of the actual village, inn, shop and archives. Loading artwork now follows the destination, with no interface baked into the images.

releaseNotes.title: Sharper surfaces, smoother travel
items: Fixed scenery trimming detaching party sprites during fast travel. Destination arrival now restores the full party and checks the destination camera before showing the scene.
Removed uneven refresh-deadline frame skipping. Small screens use appropriately sized reflection and shadow buffers, with stable high-DPI resolution and idempotent resizing.
Replaced the Map icon with a clear PixelLab parchment map and kept an opaque navy-and-gold plate on hover and keyboard focus.
Added ten new native 512-pixel PixelLab world surfaces and nine matching normal maps, covering limestone, paving, plaster, slate, oak timber, meadow turf, soil, foliage and waterfall detail.
Restored physically based lighting for buildings and terrain, with material roughness, native normal detail, wet response and surface-attached crevice shading.
Added folded leaf fans to instanced tree crowns, planted flower clusters beside clear paths and doubled world-anchored floating dust particles.
Improved water depth colour, downstream ripples, broken reflections, textured cascade flow and subtle world-space spray.
Balanced warm directional light with cool sky fill and added restrained depth-selective diorama focus while keeping the playable middle ground sharp.

releaseNotes.title: Clearer battles and roads worth exploring
items: Kept the entire sluice gate, frame and stone supports together through scene batching, reflections and visibility updates. Bren now works from the correct side of the wheel. House cutaways now include main roofs in every settlement, without reacting to projecting ornaments.
Extended every POI approach and departure road with larger outskirts, more housing plots, smooth grades and glowing outward-facing exits.
Linked persistent long sunshafts and moving sky clouds to the same world-space shadow field; lantern changes fade smoothly.

Rebuilt Equipment and Inventory with illustrated character panels, live comparisons, item inspection, recipient selection, sorting and filters. Added high-resolution PixelLab portraits and distinct item artwork.
Added purchasable accessory and off-hand fittings with real MP/defense bonuses and working equip/unequip actions.
Moved monster health bars beneath their sprites, enlarged the target arrow and added a glowing red silhouette outline that preserves enemy colours.
Kept all round participants in the turn order and marked completed, current and defeated turns instead of removing entries.
Batched grass and flower patches into fewer colour and shadow submissions while retaining individual wind, interaction and cutaway masks.

releaseNotes.title: A continuous world, a clearer journey
items: Rebuilt the title around a live Brookstead river view with the supplied gold crystal wordmark, PixelLab navigation artwork, credits and a chronological release history.
Matched the loading screen to a sharp still from the same village camera, with actual loading progress and journey tips.
Rebuilt Journal, Inventory, Party, Equipment and Settings around the navy-and-gold references, with new PixelLab frames, scenery, compass and illustrated icons.
Added character recipient tabs, inventory filters, equipment comparisons, quest history, lore/help pages and grouped settings while preserving the live game data and controls.
Made distant scenery use the foreground terrain shader, multi-cluster trees, flowers and complete house meshes; removed overlapping terrain and continued the river past the village.
Rebuilt sluice supports and separated overlapping stone caps. Fitted complete railings along all four stair flights and landings.
Added varied ground-conforming rain puddles using river artwork, reflected sky, wet edges and ripples.
Anchored sunbeams in the world and linked their brightness to large moving cloud shadows.
Retained full-resolution rendering, spatial vegetation batches, responsive laptop/phone layouts, and three-slot save, load, overwrite and delete controls.
Fixed retained terrain LOD meshes and released instance buffers across repeated travel, preventing geometry counts from growing during extended play.

releaseNotes.title: Light, weather and a clearer view
items: Replaced the extra projected character silhouettes with animated alpha-tested shadows from the actual scene light.
Aligned outdoor exploration straight ahead, with a gentle downward view closer to the battle camera.
Added dimensional overhead cloud volumes and soft depth-tested shafts sharing the moving cloud-shadow field.
Made sluice visibility and moving gate transforms independent of static scene culling.
Rebuilt rain puddles as irregular ground-conforming surfaces with ripples, sky reflections and gradual drying.
Separated wet stone, timber, foliage and character shading, removing painted-looking highlights on trees.
Removed overlapping circular ground pads at community pavilions and the relief-station title view.
Scaled the HUD for laptops, tablets and short displays, with a compact phone layout and scrollable party cards.
Improved narrow-screen menu navigation, dialogue and title layouts.
Replaced the expandable feature catalogue with this dated, readable release history.

releaseNotes.title: Initial alpha release
items: Introduced the regional Elder Light story, five companions, six story battles and four Light restorations.
Built the playable overworld, fifteen points of interest and seven interiors, with a 3D discovery atlas and fast travel.
Added the gate and pump waterworks, village routines, interactions and fifteen optional local requests.
Implemented eight-direction running, Shift sprinting, trailing companions and object clearance.
Added side-on turn-based combat, timed attack chains, skills, items, guarding, Ascension and results/growth screens.
Integrated the approved PixelLab cast, 4,878 native poses, portraits, surface textures and loading illustrations.
Added 259 ElevenLabs voice performances and 93 music, ambience and effects recordings.
Implemented inventory, equipment, shops, inn recovery and three journey slots at inns and location entrances.
Added text-only guided field lessons and the scripted opening combat tutorial.
Introduced changing time of day, weather, moving cloud shade, flowing rivers, reflections and reactive foliage.
Rebuilt the title screen with cycling live locations, save previews, deletion and overwrite confirmations.
Expanded POI approaches and exits, introduced the gold PixelLab HUD, corrected roofs and repeated building cutaways, and optimized resident navigation, reflections and sustained native rendering.
